headline: SSC results out: 690,608 students fail as pass rate drops to 62.25%
summary: Girls outperform boys in pass rate and GPA-5, while the number of zero-pass institutions has more than doubled to 312.
details: The results of the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent examinations have been published. The overall pass rate has fallen to 62.25%, with 690,608 students failing to clear the exams.
A total of 116,676 students achieved GPA-5, with girls continuing to outperform boys in both the overall pass rate and the number of GPA-5 holders.
The Dhaka Education Board topped the charts in terms of GPA-5 achievers and overall pass rate, while the Madrasa Board recorded the lowest pass rate at 55.49%.
There is a significant increase in the number of zero-pass institutions, which has jumped to 312, more than double the previous count.
On the other hand, 669 institutions recorded a 100% pass rate. Over half of the humanities students were unable to clear the exams, with 59% failing.
Approximately 1.36 million seats will remain vacant in Class 11, as a large number of students failed to qualify for college admission.
For students who are dissatisfied with their results, the education board has provided guidelines on how to apply for re-scrutiny of their marks.
caption:

The results of the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent examinations have been published. The overall pass rate has fallen to 62.25%, with 690,608 students failing to clear the exams.

A total of 116,676 students achieved GPA-5, with girls continuing to outperform boys in both the overall pass rate and the number of GPA-5 holders.

The Dhaka Education Board topped the charts in terms of GPA-5 achievers and overall pass rate, while the Madrasa Board recorded the lowest pass rate at 55.49%.

There is a significant increase in the number of zero-pass institutions, which has jumped to 312, more than double the previous count.

On the other hand, 669 institutions recorded a 100% pass rate. Over half of the humanities students were unable to clear the exams, with 59% failing.

Approximately 1.36 million seats will remain vacant in Class 11, as a large number of students failed to qualify for college admission.

For students who are dissatisfied with their results, the education board has provided guidelines on how to apply for re-scrutiny of their marks.

headline: Leaked audio: TV channels threatened with permanent shutdown over July uprising coverage
summary: Former ministers Obaidul Quader and Mohammad Ali Arafat discussed shutting down channels that reported on clashes during the student-led uprising.
details: An audio recording played in the International Crimes Tribunal-2 has revealed that former Road Transport and Bridges Minister Obaidul Quader and former Information Minister Mohammad Ali Arafat threatened to shut down TV channels that reported on clashes during the July uprising.
In the conversation, Quader told Arafat that those who do not listen should face strict action, and that no news of clashes should be aired today.

Arafat responded by stating that he had already shut down one or two channels and had warned others that any channel showing footage or photos of clashes would be declared an 'enemy of the state' and shut down for life.
Arafat further revealed that he had instructed a person at Bangabandhu Satellite to constantly monitor TV channels and shut them off immediately without needing further permission.

The case involves seven defendants, including Obaidul Quader, Mohammad Ali Arafat, and other leaders of the former regime's student and youth wings. All the accused are currently fugitives.

The audio also contains a conversation where Arafat describes the protesters as being split into 'quota movement students' and 'third-party terrorists from Jamaat-BNP' to create a narrative for the curfew decision.
